summary: The Pipeline Security Act gives formal legal authority to the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) to oversee and secure pipeline transportation and facilities against cybersecurity threats, terrorism, and other security risks. The bill requires the TSA to create guidelines, issue regulations, inspect critical facilities, engage with industry stakeholders, report to Congress every two years, and develop an internal personnel and cybersecurity strategy.

affected_groups.effect: Must officially maintain pipeline security responsibilities, create guidelines and regulations, conduct inspections, develop a personnel strategy, and report biennially to Congress.
Subject to TSA guidelines, security directives, regulations, inspections of critical facilities, and engagement during industry days.
Must conduct a review of the implementation of the act within two years.

key_provisions: Codifies the TSA's responsibility for securing pipeline transportation and facilities against cybersecurity threats and terrorism.
Requires the TSA to develop and update pipeline security guidelines and issue necessary security directives or regulations.
Mandates that the TSA inspect pipeline facilities designated as critical by owners and operators.
Requires the TSA to host at least one industry day to engage with stakeholders within one year of enactment.
Requires the TSA to submit biennial reports to specific congressional committees regarding pipeline security activities.
Directs the TSA to develop a personnel strategy assessing necessary cybersecurity expertise and resources within 180 days.
Requires the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to review the implementation of this act within two years.
missing_information: Specific funding amounts or budget appropriations allocated to carry out the personnel strategy and inspections.
Exact enforcement penalties or legal consequences for pipeline operators who fail to comply with TSA directives.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Pipeline Security Act gives formal legal authority to the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) to oversee and secure pipeline transportation and facilities against cybersecurity threats, terrorism, and other security risks. The bill requires the TSA to create guidelines, issue regulations, inspect critical facilities, engage with industry stakeholders, report to Congress every two years, and develop an internal personnel and cybersecurity strategy.
summary_detail.significance: The bill provides formal statutory backing for the TSA's ongoing role in pipeline security, standardizing oversight practices across the United States. Its score for significance reflects its establishment of formal requirements for federal oversight, industry engagement, and reporting without changing broader economic structures.
